title: Some answers regarding factorizations of finite groups
summary: In this note we answer some questions of G. M. Bergman concerning factorizations of finite groups. Such questions originated when M. H. Hooshmand asked whether, given a finite group $G$ and a factorization $|G| = n_1 \cdots n_k$, one can always find subsets $A_1, \dots , A_k$ of $G$ with $|A_i| = n_i$ such that $G = A_1 \cdots A_k$. This was Question 19.35 of the Kourovka Notebook. G. M. Bergman provided a counterexample for $k=3$, and Kabenyuk provided counterexamples for all $k \geq 3$.
